correctness.rationale: Explicit proofs: rebalancing uniqueness follows from endowment average; disjoint/nested costs commute when both fully funded; crossing construction selects a rational open interval, guarantees both complete payments, and produces a strict one-support optional-project affordance difference. Exact-rational checker traverses 2,547 support pairs up to six voters, 383,958 full-financing cost cases and witnesses for all 1,278 crossing pairs. Enumeration corroborates but is not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary full text defines the exact mechanism and gives only a concrete order-dependent four-voter example; the new mathematical iff commutativity theorem and universal three-voter downstream-selection construction are not contained in, or implied by, that example or the source proportionality results. Targeted research-record and primary-literature searches returned no stronger/equivalent coverage. Novelty remains best-knowledge with an acknowledged unindexed prior commutativity risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or abstract algebraic commutativity results for capped equal-share water-filling may entail the nested/disjoint criterion.
The theorem does not address underfunded steps or three or more preselected projects.
Self-review is not independent peer review.

value.rationale: A necessary-and-sufficient structural condition for implementation order invariance of a specific mixed participatory-budgeting mechanism resolves a motivated ambiguity; the general crossing construction shows that differences can actually change future project selection, establishing a genuine selection consequence at the smallest size. The result concerns all electorate sizes under stated full-funding conditions, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
